name: Yokkaichi

queries.query: Yokkaichi Japan official cadastral parcel map GIS land registry natural resources
queries.result: First-party discovery found the Yokkaichi official public GIS and official city cadastral-map copy/inspection information. The public GIS catalog exposes planning, roads, facilities, disaster, agricultural and sewer maps, but no public cadastral parcel layer or anonymous parcel feature endpoint was identified.

registryBasis: A city-local first-party custodian is evidenced: Yokkaichi City publishes its public GIS and official cadastral-map copy application, while the Tsu Legal Affairs Bureau identifies the Yokkaichi Branch as the local real-estate registration office. This establishes local cadastral/registry procedure evidence, not open parcel geometry access.

officialSources.observation: Official Yokkaichi public GIS portal. The visible catalog lists public facilities/points, planning regulations, building-standard roads, certified roads, archaeological sites, disaster information, agricultural land and sewer ledgers; no cadastral parcel map is listed.
Official city page describes the public GIS as a way to view planning information and warns that the overview map is not a legal boundary map.

Official Yokkaichi cadastral-map copy application form; it requests 大字/字/地番 and warns the copy does not exactly represent land shape, boundary lines or parcel-number display. No downloadable parcel geometry service is provided.
First-party Legal Affairs Bureau page identifies the Yokkaichi Branch and real-estate registration services, including inquiries and copies of maps/registration documents.

requests.outcome: HTTP 200; portal HTML and map catalog readable. No parcel layer or feature-service URL exposed in the bounded page inspection.
HTTP 200; official use-agreement shell for the planning map. The page describes overview planning data and legal/boundary limitations; no parcel schema, CRS or anonymous parcel response.
HTTP 200; route returned the agreement/application shell rather than map features because the public-use agreement was not submitted. No login, credentials, private token or bypass was attempted.
HTTP 200; official PDF application instructions read. It is a request/counter procedure, not an anonymous parcel geometry endpoint.
